items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: here I am with one of my heroes, Sonny Stitt... I still listen to Sonny Stitt, my heroes... I copied Sonny Stitt or whoever, and I had his licks

ctx.x: You had a resume though. I mean you had things that you could cite —

Well the Blood, Sweat & Tears stuff mostly. I mean arranging “Spinning Wheel” and placing top 10 in the Down Beat and Playboy polls, on alto, which I thought was, not funny, not that I couldn’t play it, but here I am with one of my heroes, Sonny Stitt, a couple of notches below or above him in the top 10 on alto. But it’s a popularity thing and not that I can’t play.

Are we getting a lot of noise from that chair? Good. Okay. I’ll cut that part out. How have you seen the business change, of jazz education in the last ten or so years because of technology. The students that come to you, they’ve grown up in this everything is available on YouTube and on Spotify and so forth. Do you notice a difference in the students?
